newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FIRST INTERNATIONAL AT KILMARNOCK FOR 87 YEARS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIRST INTERNATIONAL AT KILMARNOCK FOR 87 YEARS.

text.p: Rugby Park, the home of Scottish premier division club Kilmarnock, will stage an international match for the first time since 1910 when Scotland meet Estonia in a World Cup qualifier there on March 29.

The Scottish Football Association is using different venues for home qualifiers while the redevelopment of Hampden Park continues. They beat Sweden at Ibrox in November and Celtic's Parkhead stadium is expected to be the stage for Scotland's group two qualifier against Austria on April 2.
The last time Scotland played an international at Kilmarnock, about 50 kilometres south west of Glasgow, was on March 5, 1910 when they beat Wales 1-0.

Scotland and Estonia will place each other twice in seven weeks in February and March. On February 11 they will meet in neutral Monaco to stage the controversial replay of the "match that never was" in Tallinn on October 9 last year.
Estonia failed to turn up for the match which was abandoned three seconds after Scotland kicked off.
